While parts of southern Odisha woke up to biting cold, the state is preparing for a sharp weather shift. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rain and thunderstorm alerts across Odisha from November 19 to 21, with an orange warning for South Odisha, even as temperatures plunged in the hills.
In the last 24 hours, dry weather prevailed across the state due to the inflow of cold, dry winds from the west. This pulled night temperatures down sharply in the Koraput-Kandhamal belt. Semiliguda in Koraput district recorded the lowest minimum temperature at 10°C, making it the coldest place in Odisha. G. Udayagiri in Kandhamal followed at 11.4°C, Daringbadi at 13.5°C, Phulbani at 14.5°C, while Koraput and Nabarangpur both touched 15°C. In total, six places recorded temperatures of 15°C or below.
According to the Regional Meteorological Centre, the next 24 hours will see little change. After that, minimum temperatures are expected to rise by 2–3 degrees as moisture and rainfall activity increase.
On Wednesday, Ganjam, Gajapati and Puri districts are under a yellow warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms and winds of 40–50 km/h. Coastal Odisha and 15 adjoining districts have also been placed under yellow alert for thunderstorms and scattered rain.
From Thursday onwards, rainfall activity is set to intensify. Orange and yellow warnings will remain in force for Thursday, Friday and Saturday, with heavy to very heavy rain likely in several districts, especially in South Odisha. The change is linked to a cyclonic circulation over the Bay of Bengal.
Regional Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty said the system is being closely monitored and urged people not to panic. “The circulation is being tracked. There is no need for fear,” she stated, while advising residents to stay alert to official updates.
